gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much tool-change time and waste a full job adds. Per 1,000 tool changes, the Prusa CORE One+ INDX spends about 3.3 h swapping (12 s each) and wastes about 13 g of filament (0.013 g each). The Snapmaker U1 spends about 1.4 h (5 s each). So on a print with many colour changes, the INDX's low-waste nozzle swap adds about 1.9 h per 1,000 changes.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rival pages, 3dprinteray.com/toolchanger-printers (2026-10-14) and 3dtoolchangers.com/printers. 3dprinteray gives the inputs, about 5 s for the U1 swap and about 12 s for the INDX change, plus the XL+ cost per extra head. It never turns them into hours or grams for a whole job. It also doesn't give the INDX's 0.013 g waste per change, and neither page gives any purge or waste figure. Tom's Hardware's best-picks page came back truncated, so I couldn't check it. The per-tool prices in my fetch summaries were worked out by the fetch tool, not stated on either page.
decides: For dense multicolour work (thousands of changes per plate), this favours the U1 or Creator 5 Pro on time, since a full toolhead swaps in about 5 s. The INDX makes sense when the buyer cares more about nozzle or material variety and near-zero waste (13 g per 1,000 changes) than about speed. Its 8-tool configuration also brings the price per tool close to the budget machines: $281 assembled, $244 as a kit.
